name: Liz Truss
role: UK Prime Minister (2022); Foreign Secretary (2021-2022); MP for South West Norfolk (2010-2024)
summary: Liz Truss is a UK Conservative politician whose record centres on free markets, tax cuts, deregulation and a smaller state, along with Brexit and a hawkish stance on Russia and China. After leaving office she has argued against net zero policy and the administrative state and for leaving the ECHR, and has opposed gender self-identification.

sources.usedFor: Sections 1.2–1.3: personally defended growth-plan record and tax changes.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Described herself in her 2018 LSE lecture as a committed free marketer and argued that free enterprise lowers prices and creates growth and jobs.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her 2022 mini-budget abolished the 45p top rate (later reversed under market pressure); she wrote in 2011 in favour of a 40p top rate and said in 2022 'I do not believe that we can tax our way to growth'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In her LSE lecture she argued for cutting red tape and regulation wherever possible; her 2022 mini-budget scrapped the bankers' bonus cap.

cut-welfare.rationale: Told the LSE in 2018 that welfare changes had released millions trapped in poverty into work and that the welfare state had been holding people back; no explicit call for cuts found.

unions-good.rationale: Said strikes 'benefit no one' (2013) and told the LSE that in the 1980s unions were holding people back from jobs and that Thatcher curbed excessive union power approvingly.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted for the Strikes (Minimum Service Levels: Fire and Rescue Services) Regulations in March 2024, and opposed teacher strikes in 2013; a vote alone is medium.

public-ownership.rationale: In her 2018 LSE lecture she called Canada's 1960s years of raising taxes and nationalising businesses 'misconceived' and praised the 1990s rescue by cutting spending.

state-harmful.rationale: Stated that government has an invaluable role in education, health, infrastructure and keeping markets fair, so does not hold the state unnecessary.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Said government's role includes educating children, keeping people healthy and investing in infrastructure, beyond defence and justice, while wanting a smaller state.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted with the government for the Investigatory Powers Bill in November 2016 and for the Covert Human Intelligence Sources Bill third reading in 2020.

empower-police-military.rationale: As Foreign Secretary in June 2022 said it is right that the UK is increasing defence spending in a more insecure world.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted to legalise same-sex marriage in 2013.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reported to have voted to decriminalise abortion in Northern Ireland and abstained on buffer zone votes; mixed and second-hand.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2020 she rejected self-identification and kept the Gender Recognition Act with medical checks; in December 2023 she introduced a bill defining sex in the Equality Act as biological sex and barring state recognition of under-18 social transition.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Her December 2023 private member's bill would make sex in the Equality Act 2010 a matter of biological sex.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Popular Conservatism group she launched in 2024 pressed for tougher immigration policy, while her 2022 government planned to ease immigration to fill vacancies; mixed.

free-trade.rationale: Argued as Trade Secretary and in 2018 that open and liberal trade benefits consumers and growth; secured the UK-Australia deal and CPTPP accession.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As Trade Secretary she urged the US to stop tit-for-tat tariffs and described the opposition to trading across the world as protectionism.

limit-growth.rationale: Made growth her central objective ('growth, growth, growth') and in her 2024 book calls net zero a drag on economic growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Her 2024 book calls for abolishing the Climate Change Act, calls the drive to net zero 'unilateral economic disarmament' and says the COP summits should be cancelled.

expand-nuclear.rationale: As Prime Minister launched Great British Nuclear aiming at up to a quarter of electricity from nuclear by 2050; her book backs nuclear.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Lifted the fracking moratorium and opened about 100 North Sea licences as Prime Minister; her book says there should be fracking in the UK and that North Sea oil and gas is crucial.

experts-over-public.rationale: In 2024 she criticised the health establishment, saying the tobacco proposal came from professionals pushing a policy rather than from constituents.

central-planning.rationale: Told the LSE she wants an economy where 'it's not about the state deciding what you do, it's about you deciding' and warned that state control leads to stagnation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Supported abolishing the monarchy as a student Liberal Democrat but said in 2022 she regretted that speech almost immediately.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Regretted her 1994 abolition speech, but no stated position on hereditary titles since.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Backed Remain in 2016 but later said she was wrong; as Foreign Secretary introduced the Northern Ireland Protocol Bill against the EU's position.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Called for a British Bill of Rights in 2016, introduced the Northern Ireland Protocol Bill in 2022, and her Popular Conservatism group sought leaving the ECHR.

harm-principle.rationale: Said in April 2024 that protecting under-18s is right but protecting adults from themselves infantilises people and limits personal freedom.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Praised prudence and fiscal rules in 2018 but as PM in 2022 funded large tax cuts by borrowing.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Praised the OBR and fiscal rules in 2018, then bypassed the OBR in the 2022 mini-budget.

no-business-privileges.rationale: In 2018 argued that regulation should not protect incumbents from competition and that bright ideas should be rewarded over the biggest legal departments.

precautionary-principle.rationale: As Environment Secretary approved temporary use of neonicotinoid pesticides despite the EU ban.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Advocated a carbon tax in 2011's After the Coalition; no later position found.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Voted for the Overseas Operations Bill and for the Northern Ireland Troubles Legacy Bill second reading.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As Foreign Secretary championed NATO and Western alliance support for Ukraine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As Foreign Secretary championed NATO and Western alliance support for Ukraine.

close-ties-china.rationale: Called for reducing UK economic dependence on China, supported sanctions over Xinjiang and warned about Chinese involvement in infrastructure.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: She called Lucy Connolly's 31-month sentence for a deleted social-media post part of a 'free speech crisis' and said Britain is 'plagued with censorship'.

gender-social-construct.rationale: She rejected challenging the reality of men, women and biological sex.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: She defended inherited British values and patriotic flags.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: She advocated abandoning global administrative structures, including the COP process.

nation-first.rationale: She condemned prioritising international bodies over British people.

revolution-justified.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: She praised Britain and America for having 'developed and perfected representative democracy' and defended leaders' democratic mandates against unelected officials.

equal-outcomes.rationale: She rejected fixing equality results and instead advocated genuine equality of opportunity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: She urged government to free disruptive technological entrants from incumbent interests blocking them.

restore-past-order.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: She rejected defining people through protected groups and centred equality on individual agency and character.

national-rebirth.rationale: She urged counter-revolution to reverse decline and reclaim national greatness.

national-self-determination.rationale: At the UN she affirmed the sovereignty and right to self-determination of nations.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: She described a rigged establishment subverting elected policies.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: She affirmed dignity, humanity and fair treatment regardless of race, religion, sex or sexuality.

consent-of-governed.rationale: She objected that power has moved from elected politicians who 'can be voted out of office' to unelected independent bodies.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: She cited the 1980 Housing Act, which created the right to buy, as a reform that 'empowered over two million people to get on the housing ladder'.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: She explicitly rejected the claim that all cultures are equal.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Her latest interview called for repealing the Bank of England Act and ending unaccountable Bank power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: She praised the Queen’s ability to transcend national divisions and heal differences.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: She praised Magna Carta: even kings stand under law.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: She sought repeal of judicial constraints on elected parliamentary decisions.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: She rejected workplace quotas and diversity statements in favour of transparent, performance-based recruitment.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: She praised the US First Amendment and constitution as a 'bulwark' but wants Britain's uncodified parliamentary sovereignty restored and the Human Rights Act repealed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

parliament-supreme.rationale: She explicitly demanded restored parliamentary sovereignty.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Her farming speech supported livestock production while praising high animal-welfare standards.

corporate-influence.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Her Open Environment speech explicitly advocated valuing ecosystems as economic capital.

notes:
Changed her mind from Remain to Brexit (2016-2017), and from a student Liberal Democrat and republican to the Conservatives (1996). Hansard, vote records and her Spectator-published LSE lecture were the main primary texts; her 2024 book was seen only through quotation in DeSmog.
